body_html:
Hotels in Vietnam ask for passport details at check-in: Australia's Smartraveller advice says the hotel will need your passport details, and Canada says staff may ask to see the passport and make copies. That request is not just hotel habit: official sources describe a temporary residence declaration that foreigners must make with the local police, normally through the accommodation. Understanding what that declaration is helps separate a hotel's registration from other requests for documents, including those that may come up when hiring a motorbike.

This article draws on Vietnam's national e-visa portal and its FAQ, the U.S. Embassy in Hanoi and the governments of Australia, Canada and the UK. The portal and FAQ pages show no date, so they are described as read on 24 October 2026. No source reviewed says what a rental shop may lawfully ask for or hold, and none gives fine amounts. Rules change, so confirm details with the official source or the local police.

What the declaration is and who files it

Vietnam's e-visa portal states that foreigners temporarily residing in Vietnam must go through the person directly managing and operating the accommodation to declare their temporary residence with the local police, meaning the commune, ward or town police station. The portal also lists, among a foreigner's obligations, presenting a passport or international travel document and any residence documents to the accommodation so the declaration can be made.

The U.S. Embassy in Hanoi, on a page with no date, gives its understanding that the rule applies to all visitors, Vietnamese people included, at the police station for the place where they stay overnight. That is the Embassy's hedged reading, not a quotation of the law.

Moving between places

The e-visa FAQ says a traveller who plans to stay in several places must declare the first address where they will stay. After entering Vietnam, the declaration must be made through the accommodation's manager or operator each time the traveller changes the place of temporary residence. The portal adds that a foreigner who changes residence, or stays at an address different from the one recorded, must update the declaration under the same rules. For a rider moving between towns, this suggests each new place of stay needs its own declaration.

The 24-hour timing

Neither the portal nor the FAQ states a time limit for the declaration. The figure comes from two foreign governments. Australia's Smartraveller advice, updated on 24 September 2026, and the UK government's guidance on living in Vietnam, last updated 23 September 2025, both say foreigners must register their place of residence with the local police within 24 hours of arrival.

Hotels, private homes and your passport

SituationWhat official sources sayPublisher
Hotel stayCheck that registration is part of the normal check-in; the hotel will need the passport detailsAustralian Government Smartraveller, updated 24 September 2026
Commercial accommodationGenerally files the declaration on the guest's behalf; staff may copy the passportGovernment of Canada, last updated 19 October 2026
Private home or other non-commercial stayEither the host notifies the authorities or the guest does so at the nearest police station; failing to do so may lead to fines for both host and guestGovernment of Canada, last updated 19 October 2026
Which passportUse the passport that was used to enter VietnamAustralian Government Smartraveller, updated 24 September 2026

Holding the passport is a separate question from registering it. Smartraveller says many hotels ask foreigners to leave their passport with staff for registration, but that it is not a legal requirement for hotels to keep the passport for the length of the stay. Canada says hotels may insist on holding the passport until the guest leaves, adding that it knows of no local legal requirement for retaining it.

What ID to carry day to day

The UK government's safety and security advice, on a sub-page that shows no date, says visitors must always carry photographic ID, and that the authorities will accept a printed copy of the photo page of the passport and visa. It also advises keeping the passport safe in a hotel or other secured location and carrying both photo and digital copies. The e-visa portal lists, among foreigners' obligations, carrying a passport or international travel document, and residence documents, when travelling and presenting them when competent authorities ask. It does not say whether a copy meets that duty. The UK advice to keep the original secured and carry copies is the UK government's guidance to its own travellers, not a statement of what Vietnamese authorities accept.

What this means when a rental shop asks for documents

The same UK page gives a direct warning. It says visitors should not give their passport to others as a guarantee, naming motorcycle rental shops and landlords as examples, because they can hold it against claimed damage. It also says not to use a passport as security for hiring vehicles or as a guarantee of paying a fine for a traffic offence.

That is the UK government's advice to its own travellers, not Vietnamese law and not a statement about any particular shop. The legal duty described above runs between the foreigner, the accommodation operator and the police, and the sources reviewed do not connect it to rental shops. A hotel registering a guest and a shop asking for a document are therefore separate situations.

A plain checklist for any request for documents:

  • Ask which documents are wanted and why.
  • Ask whether looking at a document is enough, or whether anything is to be kept, and for how long.
  • Ask how and when anything kept is handed back.
  • If the bike was arranged through a hotel, ask who the contracting shop is. Motorbike Rental Through a Hotel: Identify the Contracting Shop and Support Contact covers identifying the shop and a support contact.
  • Compare the answers with the UK government advice above before handing over an original passport, and ask what else would be accepted.

For the wider booking questions, Hanoi Motorbike Rental Guide: What to Check Before Booking sets out what to check before booking.

  • Immigration Department, Ministry of Public Security, e-visa FAQs: declaring each change of residence (no date shown). https://evisa.gov.vn/faq
  • U.S. Mission Vietnam, visas and entry or exit: the Embassy's understanding of who must register (no date shown). https://vn.usembassy.gov/vietnamese-visas-and-entry-exit/
  • Australian Government Smartraveller, Vietnam: 24-hour registration, hotel check-in, passport holding (updated 24 September 2026). https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/asia/vietnam
  • Government of Canada, Vietnam travel advice: commercial and private accommodation, passport retention (last updated 19 October 2026). https://travel.gc.ca/destinations/vietnam
  • UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, living in Vietnam: 24-hour registration (last updated 23 September 2025). https://www.gov.uk/guidance/living-in-vietnam
